feed.title: Wits AHEAD · Daily briefing
feed.subtitle: News, research, video and things to read on AI, data and human ability for higher education.
feed.rights: Wits AHEAD Research Group, Wits School of Education, University of the Witwatersrand

entry.title: Gates Foundation commits 1 billion US dollars over two years to equitable AI
entry.summary:
Gates Foundation don promise at least 1 billion US dollars for di next two years to build and deliver artificial intelligence wey go fair for everybody, wit 400 million for education, 400 million for health, 100 million for agriculture and 100 million for AI training data for languages wey no dey get enough attention. Di promise come togeda wit di foundation number ten Goalkeepers report, wey dem call Make This Matter: AI, Equity and the Choice We Can't Delay.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar 6 dey ask who dey design AI wit responsibility and for who. Charity money wey big like dis, wey dem target to close di gap for di poorest regions, go decide which AI-for-education tools go reach di Global South classrooms wey Wits AHEAD dey study.

Gates Foundation · Foundation press release accompanying its Goalkeepers report

entry.title: Systematic review of 105 studies finds Africa and Oceania missing from generative AI teacher research
entry.summary:
One PRISMA-guided review of 105 peer-reviewed studies on teachers and generative AI, wey dem publish since 2023 for di top educational technology journals, find say di evidence concentrate for China, Turkey, di United States and Spain, while Africa and Oceania no dey show well at all. AI literacy, teaching knowledge and self-confidence, wey dem frame through di TPACK model, na di strongest predictors of good classroom integration, ahead of just having di tools.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar 3 cover AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education. Review wey big like dis confirm say Wits AHEAD own research on African teacher education dey fill gap wey dem don document, no be say e dey repeat wetin plenty pipo don do.

Education Sciences (MDPI) · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Stanford study finds a persistent 19% AI employment gap for young workers
entry.summary:
Stanford Digital Economy Lab report say di number of pipo wey dey work among 22 to 25 year olds for jobs wey AI dey affect pass don drop to 19% below where e for dey if e bin follow di pipo wey AI no too affect, from 15% one year before. Di gap dey happen mainly because companies dey hire less, no be say dem dey sack pipo, and e concentrate for jobs wey build on textbook-style knowledge like software engineering and customer service.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar 4 dey ask how AI dey change di road from qualification to livelihood. Dis na di clearest number-based evidence so far say entry-level graduate jobs wey build on knowledge dey shrink first, and e make di case strong for graduate capability work wey pass certificate alone.

Stanford Digital Economy Lab · University research institute report

entry.title: New Global South framework sets conditions for responsible generative AI in teaching
entry.summary:
One bibliometric and systematic review for di International Journal of Emerging Technologies in Learning trace di fast-growing research on responsible generative AI for teaching and propose one conceptual framework for di Global South. E find say di United States, China and Australia dey lead di research output, and e identify ethical awareness, trust, institutional support, infrastructure readiness and AI competence as di conditions wey shape adoption pass.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar 6 cover responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy. Dis framework give Wits AHEAD one peer-reviewed reference point to judge when generative AI adoption for Southern universities dey truly responsible, no be just available.

International Journal of Emerging Technologies in Learning (iJET) · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: PISA 2025 finds 15-year-olds who skip AI chatbots for schoolwork outscore those who rely on them, as global reading skills fall sharply
entry.summary:
Di OECD PISA 2025 results, wey come out on 8 September 2026, show say reading scores fall by 28 points across OECD countries and by 16 points among di oda countries and economies wey take part between 2015 and 2025, one of di sharpest drops since di assessment start. Di report find say 15-year-olds wey no dey use AI chatbots for schoolwork generally score higher dan di ones wey dey use am, and say more dan one in four students talk say dia classmates dey lose concentration because of digital devices for most or every science lesson.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar 5, analytics and data for education systems and decision-making, get one strong system-level signal here: one global assessment wey link heavy use of AI chatbots to weaker results, one caution wey Wits AHEAD dey weigh directly against im own pillar 1 work on generative AI for teaching and assessment.

OECD (PISA 2025 Results, Volume I) · Intergovernmental body report

entry.title: Indian researchers show synthetic student data can train dropout early-warning systems without exposing real records
entry.summary:
Researchers for Parul University for India, wey write for di Nature journal Scientific Reports, build one machine-learning framework wey train dropout early-warning models on synthetic student data before dem fine-tune am wit small share of real records. Wen dem train am only on 20,000 synthetic students across 180 courses, di model correctly identify 47.3 per cent of at-risk students by week four, and e reach accuracy score of 0.831 once dem fine-tune am wit just one fifth of real data, close to di 0.842 benchmark wey training on real data alone set.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar 2, AI and predictive analytics for student success, get one practical answer to one real problem: universities wey no fit share sensitive student records still fit build reliable retention early-warning systems, one road wey Wits AHEAD fit weigh for im own throughput and retention work.

Scientific Reports (Nature Portfolio) · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: UNESCO-ICHEI dialogue in Kathmandu charts ethical, gender-inclusive AI integration for South Asian universities
entry.summary:
UNESCO Kathmandu office, Tribhuvan University, di Asian Development Bank and UNESCO-ICHEI gada South Asian higher education leaders and government officials on 20 May 2026 to plan wetin Shafika Isaacs keynote call one inclusive and fair AI ecosystem. Di dialogue name uneven digital infrastructure, small AI skills among lecturers and scattered national policies as di region main obstacles, launch one ICHEI Nepal National Centre for Tribhuvan University for AI capacity-building, and preview one report wey dey come on digital transformation for South Asian higher education.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar 6, responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, and pillar 3, AI for STEM and teacher education, both show directly: one regional capacity-building centre and one clear commitment to full participation of girls and women for AI-related study and work offer one template wey Wits AHEAD fit weigh against Southern Africa own policy gaps.

UNESCO · UN agency article

entry.title: Cyprus study finds science teachers eager for AI but held back by confidence gaps and thin pedagogical training
entry.summary:
One Frontiers in Education study of 43 STEM teachers wey dey work for Cyprus, wey Christiana Karousiou and Maria Evagorou for di University of Nicosia lead, find say nearly 70 per cent rate technology as very important for learning results, yet only 7 per cent feel confident to use AI tools before training and 65.1 per cent no get confidence wit simulations and virtual tools. After training, di teachers see AI potential for personalised learning and automatic grading, but 83.7 per cent still talk say dem no get enough teaching knowledge to use am well and 74.4 per cent worry say e go weaken students critical thinking.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar 3, AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, dey addressed directly: di gap wey dis study document between teachers enthusiasm and dia readiness na exactly wetin Wits AHEAD own teacher-education work wan close.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: UNESCO report confronts AI's 'elephant in the room' questions for education
entry.summary:
UNESCO don publish The Algorithm in the Room, one collection of 26 think pieces on how algorithmic systems dey reshape education, wey dem release to match Digital Learning Week 2026 for Paris. Di report arrange contributions from students, educators, researchers and policymakers around six questions wey cover agency, relational development, pedagogy, cognition, governance and di future of education. E frame algorithmic systems as one urgent issue wey pipo never really address and wey dey run through education systems worldwide.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 6, responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, di report give Global South universities one structured set of governance questions to test dia own AI policies against, instead of importing frameworks wey dem build for richer systems.

UNESCO · UN agency report

entry.title: South African universities move from detecting AI use to redesigning assessment
entry.summary:
North-West University, di University of Pretoria, Stellenbosch University and Wits each dey rethink how dem dey handle generative AI, moving from detecting AI use to redesigning assessment itself. Stellenbosch stop Turnitin AI detector after dem find say e flag 61.3 per cent of work by pipo wey English no be dia first language as AI generated, against 5.1 per cent for native speakers, while North-West become di first South African university wit formal AI policy and don put more dan 3,000 students through one free AI literacy course.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar one, generative AI for teaching, assessment and integrity, dey work out for real time for South African campuses, wit direct lessons for Wits AHEAD own guidance on fair and reliable assessment.

TechCentral · Established South African technology press

entry.title: Study argues the EU AI Act requires rethinking STEM pedagogy, assessment and teacher agency
entry.summary:
One peer reviewed analysis by Konstantinos Kotsis and Georgios Stylos argue say di European Union AI Act, togeda wit generative AI growing power, require STEM educators to rebuild teaching, assessment and dia own professional role togeda, instead of adopting AI tools small small. Di authors call for critical AI literacy wey treat AI as active participant for how knowledge dey produced, process-focused assessment wey include AI use declarations, and more teacher training for AI literacy and regulatory awareness.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar three, AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, get one regulatory case study from Europe wey Wits AHEAD fit weigh against South Africa own emerging AI policy framework.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: African Development Bank and La Francophonie launch digital skills and jobs partnership in five countries
entry.summary:
Di African Development Bank and di International Organisation of La Francophonie don sign one partnership to expand digital skills training, entrepreneurship support and job pathways for young pipo and women for Benin, Cameroon, Guinea, di Democratic Republic of the Congo and Madagascar. Di agreement, wey dem sign for Paris, cover training for web and mobile development, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence and data analytics, and e build on di OIF D-CLIC programme, wey don already train nearly 19,000 young pipo. One pilot phase of twelve to twenty four months go run before any wider rollout to oda member states.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis na one concrete test of pillar four, AI, graduate capability, employability and just transitions, for French-speaking Africa, and one model wey Wits AHEAD fit point to wen e dey weigh AI skills partnerships for oda parts of di continent.

African Development Bank Group · Intergovernmental body press release

entry.title: Learning analytics study finds early-warning models plus relational feedback lift at-risk student engagement
entry.summary:
Researchers from Monash University, di University of Hong Kong and Vanderbilt University combine machine learning early warning models, wey reach prediction accuracy above 0.8 AUC on new student cohorts, wit relational feedback emails wey dem send to students wey dem flag as at risk. More dan 30 per cent of di flagged students go on to engage wit learning activities wey dem never use before within two weeks of receiving one intervention email, and most students wey dem survey want di emails to come more often dan di twice a semester schedule wey dem test.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar two, AI and predictive analytics for student success, di study show say prediction alone no dey enough: pairing am wit carefully designed, relational feedback na wetin dey move engagement, one lesson wey relate directly to Wits AHEAD own early warning work.

Journal of Learning Analytics · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Universities UK roadmap calls for AI built into every degree, with the University of Surrey as its model
entry.summary:
Universities UK don publish one Future Jobs Roadmap, wey dem draw up wit about 200 employers, business groups and universities, wey ask every UK university to put artificial intelligence inside each degree programme instead of teaching am as separate digital skills module. Di roadmap name di University of Surrey as example, where every course from foundation year to postgraduate level now carry one discipline-specific AI component, wey one academic AI trailblazer dey oversee, togeda wit one commitment to give all undergraduates access to meaningful work-based learning by 2035.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 4, graduate capability, employability and just transitions, e set out one national model for weaving AI literacy into di discipline itself instead of bolting am on, one design question wey Wits AHEAD also dey work through for curricula across di Global South.

University of Surrey · University announcement

entry.title: African Development Bank and Korea's KAIST sign three-year deal to build African AI and digital governance skills
entry.summary:
Di African Development Bank and di Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology sign one three-year cooperation agreement for Seoul on 9 September, by di side of di eighth Korea-Africa Economic Cooperation ministerial conference. Di agreement cover joint research on AI-related public policy and datasets, and training for African public officials, researchers and technical experts, and di Bank estimate say AI fit add up to one trillion dollars to Africa economy by 2035.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 5, analytics and data for education systems and decision-making, e be one concrete channel to build di public sector research and policy capacity wey African higher education and government systems need to use AI wit responsibility.

African Development Bank, reported by allAfrica · Intergovernmental body announcement

entry.title: Global survey of 45,000 students and staff finds AI use is high but guidance on using it well lags behind
entry.summary:
Di Digital Education Council AI in Higher Education Global Survey 2026, wey draw on 45,398 responses from students and faculty across 35 countries, find say 88 per cent of students and 77 per cent of faculty now dey use AI for dia studies or teaching, up sharply on 2025. Only 29 per cent of students believe say dia lecturers ready to guide dem on how to use AI well, and just 31 per cent of faculty feel say dem dey meaningfully involved for shaping dia institution AI policy.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 1, generative AI for higher education, di gap between fast adoption and slow guidance na exactly di governance and assessment integrity question wey Wits AHEAD dey track across im partner institutions.

Digital Education Council · Global survey report

entry.title: Ten-year review finds AI research in STEM education growing fortyfold since 2016, but concentrated in the Global North
entry.summary:
One bibliometric and qualitative review of 826 peer-reviewed studies wey dem publish between 2016 and 2025, wey researchers for Ecuador State University of Milagro lead, find say annual publications on artificial intelligence for STEM education rise from four to 176 over di decade, wit di United States and China producing di most output. Di review identify five main research themes, learning analytics, engineering education, AI literacy, immersive technology and generative AI, and e flag one persistent geographical imbalance wey favour di Global North, few long-term studies and weak ethical frameworks.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 3, AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, di review confirm from di research itself di gap wey Wits AHEAD exist to close, mapping where Global South research on AI for STEM teaching still thin.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Hong Kong nursing school builds a Cantonese language AI patient to train counselling skills
entry.summary:
Di Chinese University of Hong Kong Nethersole School of Nursing don build wetin e call di world first Cantonese language large language model, wey dem use as virtual elderly patient so social work and nursing students fit practise one real-time counselling technique. Di system, wey dem develop wit di technology firm Votee AI, win gold medal for di 51st International Exhibition of Inventions for Geneva, and di developers talk say training data wey build only for English leave di about 85 million Cantonese speakers worldwide poorly served by generative AI.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 1, generative AI for higher education, and pillar 6, equity, e be one concrete example of how di language behind AI training data decide who go benefit from AI-assisted teaching, one caution for institutions wey dey serve multilingual student bodies across di Global South.

Times Higher Education · Established press

entry.title: Springer Nature's journals policy chief says the real AI question in research is risk management, not disclosure alone
entry.summary:
Writing for Times Higher Education, Springer Nature head of journals policy, Ellie Gendle, argue say academic publishing don dey ask di wrong question about generative AI for research: no be whether dem use am, but how dem dey manage and disclose di risks of using am. She set out Springer Nature five principle framework of accountability, transparency, confidentiality, editorial independence and scholarly judgement, separate AI wey dem use to improve readability from AI wey shape di real findings, and cite Oxford University Press survey evidence say researchers still dey under-report dia AI use because dem fear suspicion.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 6, responsible AI, ethics and policy, e signal where di major publishers dey go on research integrity, wey relate directly to how Wits AHEAD dey frame im own guidance for postgraduate research and journal submissions.

Times Higher Education · Established press, publisher policy

entry.title: Ecuadorian study of 980 students finds integrity culture, not device rules, predicts ethical generative AI use
entry.summary:
One study of 980 students for two Ecuadorian universities use structural equation modelling to identify wetin dey predict ethical use of generative AI for coursework. Academic integrity and transparency na di strongest predictor, ahead of technical literacy, critical thinking and institutional guidance, and di model explain 44 per cent of di variance for ethical AI use.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 1, generative AI for higher education, e suggest say Wits AHEAD suppose back institutional integrity culture and transparent disclosure norms instead of relying on device bans or detection software alone.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: South African study proposes 'early success indicators' in place of deficit based at-risk student labels
entry.summary:
Researchers Philokuhle Majozi and Kgadi Mathabathe propose one data-informed 'early success indicators' framework for one South African university, mapping di key moments across di student journey from enrolment to final assessment to flag where support dey needed. Instead of di deficit language of 'at-risk' students, di framework ask wetin conditions must dey in place for students to succeed, and e require institutional collaboration, one culture of data transparency and timely, targeted interventions.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 2, AI and predictive analytics for student success, e offer one South African, strengths-based alternative to di usual early warning models wey Wits AHEAD fit draw on directly.

Journal of Student Affairs in Africa · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Cape Town to host Times Higher Education's World Academic Summit for the first time in Africa
entry.summary:
Di University of Cape Town, wit di University of Bristol and Times Higher Education, go host di THE World Academic Summit from 29 September to 1 October 2026, di first time di summit dey hold for di African continent. Wit di theme 'Knowledge, justice and futures: Universities in the age of intelligence', di programme get four strands, including ethical AI, access and innovation, and di organisers talk say dem build di agenda to put African and Global South perspectives inside di structure, no be as afterthought.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 6, responsible AI, ethics and policy, and pillar 5, systems and decision making, di summit bring di global debate on AI and universities come South Africa, one chance for Wits AHEAD to engage directly, for im own doorstep, wit global higher education leadership.

University of Cape Town · University announcement

entry.title: African universities confront AI's impact on jobs and learning at Dar es Salaam summit
entry.summary:
Di University of Dar es Salaam and Michigan State University open di 2026 Alliance for African Partnership annual meeting on 16 September, and e go run till 22 September under di theme 'Reimagining Higher Education for Africa's Future: Leadership, Innovation and Global Partnerships'. Deputy Vice Chancellor for Research Professor Nelson Boniface talk say African universities must connect knowledge to society challenges as dem dey face questions wey generative AI raise for assessment and research. One public dialogue on 'AI and the Future of Work' bring higher education, technology and private sector voices togeda on 17 September.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis na one rare pan-African, university-led forum wey put AI effect on jobs and learning for di same agenda as leadership and partnerships, and e speak directly to Pillar 4 concern wit graduate capability, employability and just transitions.

The Citizen (Tanzania), Alliance for African Partnership Annual Meeting 2026 · Established press

entry.title: World Bank convenes developing-country policymakers at Seoul AI-in-education academy
entry.summary:
Di World Bank Education and Skills Global Practice run one Global EdTech Policy Academy on Artificial Intelligence for Seoul from 31 August to 4 September 2026, wit di Government of South Korea, di United Kingdom Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office and di Mastercard Foundation. Policymakers work through online preparation, intensive sessions, field visits and peer learning to build country-specific AI strategies and implementation blueprints, drawing on one curated evidence toolkit of more dan 160 resources.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis na exactly di systems-level capacity building wey Pillar 5 dey track: how education ministries dey turn AI evidence into governance structures and implementation plans, wey relate directly to how African and oda Global South systems dey build dia own AI strategies.

World Bank, Global EdTech Policy Academy on Artificial Intelligence · Intergovernmental body

entry.title: Technology acceptance study finds strong AI adoption among South African university students
entry.summary:
Researchers from di Durban University of Technology and Mangosuthu University of Technology survey 216 students for one historically disadvantaged South African institution using one extended Technology Acceptance Model, wey dem publish for Frontiers in Education on 3 September 2026. Perceived ease of use strongly predict perceived usefulness (correlation of 0.728) and usefulness predict actual AI use (correlation of 0.647), while attitudes wey subjective norms shape also predict adoption; differences show by study level and faculty but no by gender, age or race.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis na one of di few adoption studies wey focus on one historically disadvantaged South African institution, and e give Pillar 1 concrete local evidence on how ease of use and social norms dey drive generative AI use for teaching and assessment.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Journal of International Students paper frames AI adoption as a test of equitable internationalisation
entry.summary:
Writing for di Journal of International Students on 29 August 2026, Bindiya Jain of Poornima University propose one AI and Sustainable Internationalisation Framework wey separate system-level, policy-driven AI adoption from tool-level, practitioner-driven adoption for higher education. Di paper argue say deliberate attention to both levels, tied to di Sustainable Development Goals on quality education and reduced inequality, na wetin dey stop AI adoption from widening di digital divide for developing economies.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis give Pillar 6 one conceptual framework to judge whether one AI adoption decision, for Wits AHEAD or anywhere else for di Global South, dey close or widen educational inequality.

Journal of International Students · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Inside Higher Ed: universities are going all in on AI while the independent evidence base is described as almost nonexistent
entry.summary:
Kathryn Palmer report say OpenAI don sell more dan 700,000 licences to institutions including di California State University system, yet researchers for MIT, Stanford and Ithaka S+R talk say rigorous, large-scale studies of wetin AI dey do for learning no dey and dem no likely come soon, partly because di models dey change every few months. One community college study wey di piece cite find say access to large language models without guidance dey counterproductive.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Di gap between buying and evidence na exactly di space wey Pillar 1 dey work: designing studies of AI use for real courses, wit African students and contexts, wey institutions fit act on before di next licence renewal.

Inside Higher Ed · Established higher education press

entry.title: Chilean universities build and pilot a student-facing learning analytics app for first-year high-risk courses
entry.summary:
One team wey Universidad de Concepción lead interview 14 lecturers and run 19 focus groups wit 140 students for three Chilean universities, den design one learning analytics application inside di learning management system wey give students, no be lecturers, one view of dia own learning data across Zimmerman three phases of self-regulation. Two pilots wit 267 first-year students for high-risk courses produce higher perceived usefulness and ease of use dan one earlier version. Di authors describe di findings as preliminary and hypothesis-generating.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Most early-warning systems point data at advisers; dis one point am at di student. For Pillar 2, one student-facing design na promising route to retention for first-year gateway courses, and di Chilean context dey close to our own for scale and resources.

Frontiers in Psychology · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Somali researchers argue for AI literacy as a foundational competency across secondary and tertiary education
entry.summary:
Authors from Jamhuriya University of Science and Technology, Salaam University, East Africa University and di Benaadir Research, Consultancy and Evaluation Centre argue say Somalia no suppose ban generative AI and no suppose adopt am without safeguards. Drawing on recent research and policy documents, dem set out uses for language support, drafting and tutoring side by side wit di risks of hallucination, bias, plagiarism and privacy, and dem name teacher professional development, curriculum revision, assessment reform and ethical guidance as di implementation priorities.

Why e matter for AHEAD: One policy argument wey dem write from inside one of di continent most constrained education systems, for one peer-reviewed venue, dey rare and valuable for Pillar 6. E show di responsible-AI agenda dey set from di Global South instead of imported.

Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence · Peer-reviewed perspective article

entry.title: Meta-analysis of 35 experimental studies finds generative AI improves undergraduate learning outcomes, with effects that depend on how it is used
entry.summary:
Researchers for Zhejiang University of Technology, Nanjing Normal University and East China Normal University pool 35 experimental and quasi-experimental studies wey dem publish between 2022 and 2024. Generative AI get one large positive effect on professional skills (g = 0.72) and moderate effects on academic performance (g = 0.46) and emotional attitude (g = 0.44). Intervention duration, teaching model and di way students interact wit di tool moderate di effects, and di authors warn say subgroup results rest on small samples.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis na di kind of pooled evidence wey Pillar 1 need wen e dey advise on assessment and teaching design, and e land for di same week wey United States experts describe di independent evidence base as almost nonexistent. Di moderators, no be di headline effect, na wetin matter for course design.

Journal of Computer Assisted Learning (Wiley) · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Education ministers adopt a joint statement to keep education a common good in the age of AI
entry.summary:
More dan 25 ministers and designated representatives adopt one joint statement for UNESCO headquarters for Paris on 8 September 2026, for di opening of Digital Learning Week. E set out eight priorities: public-interest AI systems wey pipo fit audit, protection of learners critical thinking, teacher agency, age-appropriate design, educational data wey dem govern for di public interest, equity wey dem build into design, full costing before adoption, and national and regional governance capacity. UNESCO also release im second annual survey of UNESCO Chairs on AI for higher education.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis na di clearest intergovernmental statement so far say AI for education na matter of public decision and accountability, and e name data governance, equity and total cost of ownership as policy questions. E anchor Pillar 6 and give African ministries and universities one shared reference point.

UNESCO, Digital Learning Week 2026 · Intergovernmental body

entry.title: UNESCO IESALC: AI is in use at 87 per cent of surveyed universities in Latin America and the Caribbean, but only 26 per cent have a formal strategy
entry.summary:
One study of 200 higher education institutions for 19 countries, wey dem launch for Digital Learning Week, find AI in use for at least one area for 87 per cent of institutions and for teaching and learning for 74 per cent, mostly through general-purpose tools. Only 26 per cent get formal AI strategy, about half of students report confusion about wetin use dey acceptable, and private institutions dey ahead of under-resourced public ones for planning, staff training and governance.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Di pattern of fast adoption and slow governance, wit one widening gap between well-resourced and public institutions, mirror wetin we dey see for Southern Africa. One similar institutional survey for di SADC region na natural Pillar 6 project, and di finding on student confusion speak directly to assessment policy.

UNESCO IESALC · Intergovernmental body (UNESCO institute)

entry.title: 'Don't walk alone': Prof. Mwenda Ntarangwi on collaboration, AI and the future of African higher education
entry.summary:
Dem record am for di Collaborative Kigali convening ahead of im Nairobi East Africa Hub meeting for October 2026: collaboration, hub progress and technology role for African higher education.

Why e matter for AHEAD: African leadership on exactly di collaborative, cross-institution model wey AHEAD build on.

The Education Collaborative, with the Vice-Chancellor of USIU-Africa · Vice-Chancellor, USIU-Africa; Education Collaborative convening

entry.title: University of Leicester gives Microsoft 365 Copilot to all 21,000 students and 4,000 staff
entry.summary:
From September 2026 every student and staff member for Leicester get full Copilot access across Microsoft 365, paired wit compulsory digital-skills modules wey dem must complete for Blackboard before access open. Manchester announce one similar whole-institution rollout for January.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Whole-institution AI provision change di baseline for academic integrity, assessment design and equity of access. E be one live test case for Pillar 1 and one benchmark wey dem go use measure South African universities.

University of Leicester · University announcement

entry.title: Are graduates prepared for the AI era?
entry.summary:
Working It editor Isabel Berwick look at how institutions worldwide dey help graduates into first jobs, and di tools and skills wey now dey drive one successful search.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Di graduate-transition question of Pillar 4, told from di employer and graduate side.

Financial Times, Working It · Financial Times

entry.title: Youth unemployment (15 to 34) rises to 47.4% in the second quarter of 2026
entry.summary:
Di official youth unemployment rate increase by 1.5 percentage points to 47.4% for Q2 2026. Unemployed youth rise by 264,000 to 5.0 million while employed youth fall by 40,000 to 5.6 million.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis na di single defensible figure wey di group dey use for graduate pathways and just transitions. Pillar 4 dey ask how AI dey reshape di road from qualification to livelihood for exactly dis group.

Statistics South Africa, Quarterly Labour Force Survey Q2 2026 · National statistics office

entry.title: Nigeria's AI education revolution: how AI is reshaping learning, from the University of Lagos
entry.summary:
Education experts for UNILAG on how AI dey shape classrooms and academic work, and di call for guidance, regulation and responsible use.

Why e matter for AHEAD: From one partner institution for di group footprint, and squarely on Pillar 6.

News Central TV · Pan-African news channel

entry.title: World Development Report 2026: The Promise of Artificial Intelligence
entry.summary:
Di Bank first dedicated assessment of AI for low- and middle-income countries, wey dem frame as adopt, adapt, advance. Middle-income countries make up half of ChatGPT traffic within six months of launch, faster spread dan any earlier general-purpose technology, yet di report set out di electricity, connectivity and data conditions wey must dey met before AI go improve public services.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Di report na di policy frame wey funders go use for di next five years. AHEAD Global South, capability-first stance na direct response to im adopt-adapt-advance agenda.

World Bank · Intergovernmental flagship report

entry.title: Still emerging: understanding generative AI use in higher education
entry.summary:
One empirical study of how students and academics dey actually use generative AI, wey find say practice still no settle and institutions dey support am unevenly.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Useful comparator for di group own bibliometric and survey work under Pillar 1.

Frontiers in Education, peer-reviewed · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Reinventing teaching after the introduction of AI
entry.summary:
One computing professor on wetin teaching dey for wen AI fit do di assignments, drawing on years for di classroom.

Why e matter for AHEAD: One clear statement of di teaching redesign problem wey dey di heart of Pillar 1.

TEDx Talks, Prof. Amy Bruckman (Georgia Tech) · TEDx; Regents' Professor, Georgia Institute of Technology
